title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo
tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

faults.what: Residual blur and blocky smoothing remain visible in the chest fur, legs, and grass, although the face is noticeably clearer.

judge.summary: The dog is recognisably preserved and noticeably clearer, with natural-looking improvements but some remaining blur and unverified delivery dimensions.

must_haves.item: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
must_haves.why: The dog's appearance, seated pose, head position, open mouth, paws, and tail placement are preserved.

must_haves.item: The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
must_haves.why: The eyes, nose, muzzle, tongue, ears, and paw outlines are more distinct than in the source.

must_haves.item: Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
must_haves.why: The enhancement remains restrained, with no pronounced halos or decorative additions, though some fur still looks smoothed.

must_haves.item: The background and full original framing are preserved.
must_haves.why: The same lawn, trees, background structures, and full square composition remain visible without apparent cropping.

must_haves.item: The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.
must_haves.why: The square aspect ratio is preserved, but the delivered file's actual pixel dimensions cannot be verified from the displayed image or filename.
